newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks lose steam after recent rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks lose steam after recent rally.

text.p: Tokyo stocks were dealt a setback on Wednesday as profit-talking emerged to send the key Nikkei average down after big gains over the last two trading days. But brokers said that the index is likely to be supported at around 21,000 where investors' buying is said to be positioned.
The key Nikkei 225 average closed down 153.84 points or 0.72 percent at 21,156.75. Its December futures shed 140 points to finish at 21,200.
"Since the average had shot up for a couple of days, activity slowed today," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
Shares of paper and pulp companies slipped across the board, dragged down by expectations that their corporate earnings are expected to be sluggish, traders said.

New Oji Paper Co Ltd fell 26 yen to end at 820, while Honshu Paper Co Ltd also lost 26 yen to close at 670. Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd dipped 11 yen to end at 659. Mitsubishi Paper Paper Mills Ltd slipped 26 yen to 584.
Shares of Sanwa Bank Ltd jumped 70 yen to close at 2,060 on news that the issue will be included in the key 225-share Nikkei average from September 24, traders said.
The second section index fell 2.60 points to close at 2,108.01, with 15.63 million shares traded.
But the over-the-counter (OTC) index gained 5.15 points to 1,570.94.
